CANONICAL_NAME.value: biRISC-V next-PC / branch prediction unit (biriscv_npc.v: BTB, bimodal or gshare, RAS; Ultra-Embedded)

VERSION.value: github.com/ultraembedded/biriscv master as of 2026-09-12 (commit in hashes); file src/core/biriscv_npc.v

value.lineage: Dynamic branch prediction (Smith 1981 bimodal; McFarling 1993 gshare; Yeh & Patt two-level) as one Verilog module inside a small dual-issue RISC-V core: a branch target buffer, a bimodal/gshare pattern table, a return-address stack. The DECISION machinery is small and its state (counters, history) is exposed; the vault's picorv32 has no predictor at all -- this is the contrasting design point.

value.built_to: guess the next instruction address before the branch resolves, so the pipeline never waits
value.pressure: pipeline depth (a wrong guess costs a flush), tiny tables, hidden program behaviour
value.success_means: misprediction rate falls to a few percent on loops; the RAS predicts returns exactly

value.pressure: hard timing bound (one guess per cycle), bounded table memory, hidden state (program control flow)
value.failure_condition: aliasing in the pattern table makes two branches poison each other's counters
